title: The Saint Louis Bank Robbery
segments: Get it a row?
Be for yourself here.
Okay.
Your father.
I'm John Egan.
Oh, but you know?
I'm not exactly.
He's all right, John.
When were you inside?
What?
Look, I said he was all right.
Well, I've never been to prison, sir.
What are you, some kind of college boy?
No.
It's just a letter.
What is this, anyway?
You've been on a job before.
No, sir.
Nice going.
Two days notice what do you want.
I don't like going out with somebody I don't know.
I know him. I know him since he's a kid.
And drive OK and he's got the nerve.
You know what this job means to me?
He's all right. Let's get to what we're here for.
This looks like a good one. Never been touched. No bank guard.
Good location.
Five streets come right in here at this corner.
Two up and lead directly to the highway.
We won't be on any one of them after six blocks, but they'll have to watch it.
All those streets they'll be lucky if they get our direction.
Oh, oh, are we here?
Don't mean nothing.
Father, how about the money?
Fingers is Friday.
They do a big payroll business and have to have cash.
How much do you think, John?
100,000 or more?
And a tail?
That's right.
We don't fool with the vaults.
What about the split?
The usual 10% of the finger, the rest we cut down the minute.
My lawyer's going to love me.
What about fuzz?
It's good location.
They haven't had a bank job in 20 years.
Lots of fat crops and lots of old.
Can you bankroll us?
I'll take care of William Me, but you too will have to get your own eating money.
Why don't we go?
I'm not sure.
Maybe a week from Friday.
Maybe longer.
It's a lot to do.
It's cutting in clothes for me.
When'd you try?
Three weeks?
My lawyer wants it on the line before he does anything.
You have plenty of time.
What do you want us to do, John?
Here's the schedule.
We case it two hours every morning for the next five days.
You each have four 15-minute shifts.
I don't mind if you overlap a little,
but I don't want you hanging around too much.
And you know what to look for.
Scout cars, beat men, wind the money trucks in, traffic, anything unusual.
It's all down in the schedule.
You get those plates?
I have time.
Well, that's all right.
We'll let George try.
That's a good idea.
All right, with you, Georgie Boy.
Here it is. Is that all?
One thing more. No women.
You have the brains you were born with. You ought to know it.
What about Willie? You think you can stand it?
I'm in it, Gino. This is my last one. I don't want it come up.
Don't worry. I'll read a book or something.
And, hungry. Is that all?
Look around, father.
Listen, what's this you want me to do?
I didn't know worry about...
Look, Gino, I told you before I came down here.
I said I'd drive and that's all. You told him that.
Relax.
Okay, but that's all I'm going to do.
I heard you.
You got any money?
No, I thought you said you could take care of it.
I've got enough.
Great. I don't have any just a couple of bucks.
You know, Anne lives here.
So what?
Of course I go get the room.
After you get through with Eagan, why don't you go see it?
No.
Try and get 50.
Hundred of these, swing it.
I wouldn't ask her for anything.
Tell her it's for me.
Look, Georgie, this ain't the unit of the city.
You got to do some things you don't like.
I don't want to see her do you know.
I never blamed you for what happened did I?
I'm her brother and I never blamed you.
You know you wouldn't look so good preaching me a servant.
I got family feelings like anybody else.
I don't think I'd ask you that ain't choice.
Thanks. Look you got to pull your own weight.
You want to miss a chance at 20,000 because we haven't got a lousy 50 bucks.
I wouldn't know what to say to him.
You ready for it?
Yes, sir.
See you later.
Let's go.
I want a Missouri license.
One that's kind of banged up, not too easy to read.
Look, Mr. Egan, I don't know what Geno told you about me,
but I didn't come here to be a petty thief.
I said I'd drive a car, and that's all.
Is that right?
Well, I know it sounds funny,
But I'm no thief.
Look, father, you're going to be our wheel man.
Our neck depends on you.
Yes, sir.
I'll take care of my end.
I just don't see why I have to do something that somebody else could do better.
I want to see your work.
Now do you get out?
Or do we get another man?
